title: Stability of analytic fields with residue or value transcendence
statement: Let $k\subseteq E$ be complete fields with compatible nontrivial nonarchimedean real absolute values, with $k$ algebraically closed [def-weil-field]. For any such field $F$ put $F^\circ=\{a:|a|\le1\}$ [def-trf-valuation-ring], $\widetilde F=F^\circ/\{a:|a|<1\}$ and $\Gamma_F=|F^\times|\subset\mathbf R_{>0}$. For $z\in E$ write $k(z)^\wedge$ for the closure of the subfield generated by $k$ and $z$. Assume $E\ne k$ and $E$ is finite over $k(y)^\wedge$ for some $y\in E$. Assume either $\widetilde E/\widetilde k$ has transcendence degree one and $\Gamma_E=\Gamma_k$, or $\widetilde E=\widetilde k$ and $\Gamma_E/\Gamma_k$ has rational rank one. Here rational rank means the dimension after tensoring the abelian group with $\mathbf Q$. For every finite extension $H/E$ with an extending nonarchimedean absolute value, one has $$[H:E]=[\Gamma_H:\Gamma_E]\,[\widetilde H:\widetilde E].$$ In particular both indices are finite. The valuation and residue notation for $H$ has the same meaning as for $E$.

source.place: Theorem 6.3.1(iii), printed pp. 48–49; Cartesian means the degree formula of §6.1, p. 36 and §2.1, p. 9.

proof.text: Use [lem-trf-valued-finite-ramification-calculus] for completeness, finite invariants and multiplicativity. Put $p=\operatorname{char}(\widetilde k)$. If $p=0$, its defect formula gives the result. Suppose $p>0$. We first prove that every finite extension $F/E$ has a tame rational parameter. It is finite over the given $k(y)^\wedge$ and has the same residue/value type by the calculus, so [lem-trf-analytic-type-alternatives] applies to $F$.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 6.3.1, first paragraph, printed p. 49; §6.1 opening and Propositions 6.1.1, 6.2.4.

proof.text: In residue type choose a separating residue coordinate $u$ and lift $z$; in value type choose $z$ with $\Gamma_F=\Gamma_k|z|^{\mathbf Z}$, using [lem-trf-analytic-type-alternatives]. Put $J=k(z)^\wedge$; [lem-trf-analytic-parameter-finiteness] makes $F/J$ finite. In residue type, normalizing a polynomial by a coefficient of maximal norm shows that its reduction at transcendental $u$ is nonzero, so $\widetilde J=\widetilde k(u)$ and $\Gamma_J=\Gamma_k$. In value type distinct monomials have distinct norms (divisibility of $\Gamma_k$ rules out $|z|^n\in\Gamma_k$), giving $\Gamma_J=\Gamma_F$ and $\widetilde J=\widetilde k$. Approximation within the norm of a nonzero element, and within distance $<1$ of a unit, preserves these descriptions on completion. Thus $\widetilde F/\widetilde J$ is separable and $\Gamma_F=\Gamma_J$. The unramified residue lift in [lem-trf-valued-finite-ramification-calculus] gives $J\subseteq U\subseteq F$ with $U/J$ unramified and $F/U$ immediate; its degree is a power of $p$.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 6.3.1, first paragraph, printed p. 49; §6.1 opening and Propositions 6.1.1, 6.2.4.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-valued-tame-prime-tower](1), choose finite tame $U^\prime/U$ so that $FU^\prime/U^\prime$ has a tower of degree-$p$ steps. Since $U/J$ is tame, $U^\prime/J$ is tame. If the tower is nontrivial its first step is immediate: $FU^\prime/U^\prime$ is immediate by [lem-trf-valued-finite-ramification-calculus]. By [lem-trf-immediate-prime-polynomial-obstruction] that step gives $a,b\in U^\prime$ with positive unattained polynomial infimum $s$ and $|pb|<s$. This contradicts [lem-trf-analytic-critical-polynomial-minimum] for $U^\prime/J$. Hence $FU^\prime=U^\prime$. Thus $F/U$ is tame as an intermediate extension and immediate; the tame degree formula forces $F=U$. We have proved $F/J$ unramified, in particular tame, without using the parent uniformization theorem.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 6.3.1, first paragraph, printed p. 49; §6.1 opening and Propositions 6.1.1, 6.2.4.

proof.text: For any finite $F/E$, Step 3 exhibits $F$ as a tame finite extension of a completed rational type-2/3 field. An immediate degree-$p$ extension of $F$ would again yield the unattained polynomial infimum of [lem-trf-immediate-prime-polynomial-obstruction], contradicted by [lem-trf-analytic-critical-polynomial-minimum]. Therefore no finite $F/E$ admits such an extension. Apply [lem-trf-valued-tame-prime-tower](2) to $E$: every finite $H/E$ has defect one. By the finite invariants and definition of defect in [lem-trf-valued-finite-ramification-calculus], this is precisely the required formula, with both indices finite.
